crosswalk.needed: yes, by the crosswalk stage. The two zips are the originals; the extracted files are rebuilt from them by ensure_inputs.py
crosswalk.purpose: FDA NDC directory and the openFDA NDC listing: route, dosage form, labeler name and active substances for every product code
crosswalk.restore: the zips are kept; ensure_inputs.py extracts the rest. To refetch the zips: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cder/ndctext.zip and https://download.open.fda.gov/drug/ndc/drug-ndc-0001-of-0001.json.zip

enforcement.needed: no: the counts are in results/recall_match_level.json. Small enough to keep
enforcement.purpose: openFDA drug enforcement (recall) reports, used for the recall co-occurrence counts

nadac.needed: no: that check is not a pipeline stage and its output is in results/RESULTS_nadac.json
nadac.purpose: National Average Drug Acquisition Cost, yearly files: unit prices used in the spending robustness check
nadac.restore: download the yearly NADAC files from the dataset page into aux/ as nadac_<year>.csv

parts.needed: yes. These are committed to this repository: 12 MB that replaces 5 GB of raw CSVs for every purpose except rebuilding them
parts.purpose: the aggregated per-year panel parts every panel stage reads
parts.restore: committed; or rebuild with scripts/build_sdud_parts.py from the raw yearly files
parts.source: derived from the SDUD yearly files by scripts/build_sdud_parts.py

sdud_raw_in_window.needed: only to rebuild data/sdud_parts, which is committed to this repository
sdud_raw_in_window.purpose: Medicaid State Drug Utilization Data, 2016 to 2026Q1: the raw yearly files the panel is built from

sdud_raw_pre_window.needed: no: the panel starts at 2016Q1. Kept originally for a feasibility check on earlier history
sdud_raw_pre_window.purpose: Medicaid State Drug Utilization Data, 1991 to 2015

spl.needed: no: the establishment analysis is not a pipeline stage and its output is in results/RESULTS_establishments.json and RESULTS_prodestab.json
spl.purpose: DailyMed Structured Product Labeling documents, one per set id: manufacturing establishment names behind the labeler codes
spl.restore: the set ids are kept in Research/aux_spl_setids_full.txt; fetch each as https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/services/v2/spls/<setid>.xml

research_root_note: Paths are relative to the folder that holds this repository and the raw-data folders (sdud, aux, crosswalk, enforcement), which the pipeline calls RESEARCH_ROOT.
revision_caveat: CMS revises published SDUD files in place; the 2020 and later filenames carry an updatedJuly2026 suffix for that reason. A re-downloaded file may not match these hashes. The committed data/sdud_parts, not the raw CSVs, is what makes the published numbers reproducible.
